author: Claude + Gemini 3.1 Pro draft, reviewed and rewritten by Claude
basis: New mission, no workbook source. Facts: 2017 '20-30-50' legal target for 2025 (Electricity Act revision); 2024 generation mix 42.4% gas / 39.3% coal / 11.6% renewables / 4.2% nuclear (288 TWh, MOEA/EIA-sourced reporting); solar PV target 20GW by 2025 vs ~14.3GW end-2024 / ~15GW end-2025 (EnergyTrend, pv magazine, ICC Tainan); offshore wind target 5.7GW by 2025 vs ~4.6-4.9GW actual (RECCESSARY, Taiwan News, Norton Rose Fulbright); Taiwan ranked 3rd globally for new offshore wind added in 2025 and 5th for total capacity; MOEA reset the 20% deadline to November 2026 (Eco-Business); wind generation +66% 2023->2024, solar ~45%/wind ~31% of renewable mix; 2050 net-zero pathway targets 60-70% renewables by 2050, 40-55GW installed capacity vs 29GW targeted for 2025 (National Development Council); TSMC ~9% of national electricity (SDxCentral/TrendForce). Register per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md. Drafted with Gemini 3.1 Pro, then substantially rewritten by Claude for CEFR band conformance, factual precision and tone (softened one overstated 'existential threat' claim in the original draft).

slides.1: Look at the new wind turbines on our west coast. See the solar panels on school roofs. Is Taiwan really turning green fast, or is that just talk?
slides.2: SDG 7 means clean, safe, modern energy for everyone. This talk is not about climate change. It is about our energy targets, and whether we hit them.
slides.3: In 2017, Taiwan made a new law for 2025. Renewables should reach 20 percent. Coal should be 30 percent, and gas 50 percent. Today we test that 20 percent number.
slides.4: Look at Taiwan's real numbers from 2024. Clean energy reached only 11.6 percent. The target was 20 percent. Coal and gas still make over 80 percent of our power.
slides.5: Our solar goal was 20 gigawatts by 2025. We only built about 15. The work is slow. Land fights and strict rules cause long delays for new panels.
slides.6: We wanted 5.7 gigawatts by 2025. We only reached 4.9. New turbines take too long to build, because costs are high and parts are hard to get.
slides.7: We missed our own goal, but we still did well. Taiwan added more new wind power than most countries in 2025. We now rank third in the whole world.
slides.8: You can see the difference when you travel. Solar panels now sit on school roofs and over fish ponds. Wind power grew fast too. It is much bigger than before.
slides.9: The government did not cancel the target. They just moved the deadline to November 2026. This new date sounds far away, but we still need much more power.
slides.10: How can we fix this? Instead of making solar firms wait for years, Taiwan must change the rules. Leaders should make land permits faster for everyone.
slides.11: For wind power, we must bring investors back. Instead of running small auctions, Taiwan should offer bigger, safer deals. This could help pay for rising costs.
slides.12: We can also try new energy, like hydrogen and heat from the earth. Instead of only using wind and sun, we should test these too. New tech may take longer.
slides.13: Our chip factories use huge amounts of power. Global buyers want green power for their chips. Without it, they may look elsewhere. That is a real risk for Taiwan.
slides.14: We must meet the new 2026 date. If we miss it again, investors may lose trust. Less trust means higher costs, and that stops more new projects.
slides.15: This problem needs more than money to fix. If we build wind farms fast, local towns feel the change first. People near the turbines do not always get the power.
slides.16: So this problem is not only about money. If we only chase one number, we lose people's trust. The real test is hitting the goal, and keeping that trust too.
slides.17: To wrap up, we made real progress. We built new turbines and reached a top world ranking. But our real numbers are still far from our own legal target.
slides.18: This matters to you right now. You are Taiwan's future engineers. You will build the grids and the batteries. Your work can finally close this big energy gap.
slides.19: Let's look at the facts closely. Do not just ask what leaders promised. Ask what they actually built. Join local talks about where new solar farms should go.
slides.20: Remember one last thing before we go. The target date may move again someday. But our green destination must never, ever change. Let's finish this whole job together.
